result.graft: From C: also allow scrim-tap/swipe-down to dismiss the sheet and keep editing, as a secondary path to A's explicit Keep editing action.
result.defense: A is the only proposal that explicitly satisfies every criterion: persistent Send in the same place in all frames, no Done, dimmed Send for missing/invalid recipients, and exactly one conditional close sheet. Its explicit Keep editing removes any dead end when reopening or closing an edited draft. B fails the stated one-sheet requirement, does not state dimming, and replaces a deliberate choice with transient toast recovery—risking unwanted autosaved drafts, a missed Delete window, and extra autosave/toast engineering. C is a strong, native runner-up, but as written it omits dimming and makes Keep editing discoverable only via the scrim; on this small display and for non-expert users that hidden gesture is weaker than A's labelled action, despite C's cleaner two-button sheet.

Proposal A directly satisfies every acceptance criterion with the lowest risk and highest usability: it places the Send arrow in every compose frame, removes the ambiguous Done capsule, dims Send when recipients are missing or invalid, and unifies the two conflicting close prompts into a single sheet ('Save draft / Discard / Keep editing') triggered on X only when edits exist. Proposal B fails the 'one close sheet' criterion, clutters Drafts when users miss the transient delete toast, and introduces a new floating toast state on the return view that risks violating glass-group constraints. Proposal C is close to A, but omitting an explicit 'Keep editing' / 'Cancel' button and relying solely on tapping the scrim deviates from native SwiftUI confirmationDialog behavior and harms discoverability and accessibility.
